note: APAP only, as before: Banreservas answered 403, Banco Popular Dominicano's site sits behind Incapsula, and BHD's site loads its pages by script and gives no tariff to a plain request; APAP's own tariff page lists its documents by script too, so only the Familiar card's tariff, already known, could be read. Asociación Popular de Ahorros y Préstamos' tariff for its Tarjeta de Crédito Familiar (7 October 2026), read in full: the card's 7,500-peso issue charge is applied yearly over the card's life, 2,500 pesos a year (the renewal the same); purchases and cash advances in pesos bear 60% a year; a cash advance (and a casino, crypto, currency or app transfer charge) costs 6.25%; a late payment on a peso balance costs 1,200 pesos and going over the limit 800. The optional insurance and the Cuotas Más Límite instalment line on the same card aren't written. No minimum payment, grace period or foreign transaction fee is stated. Wave 4 (30 October 2026) added Scotiabank República Dominicana, one of the country's large card issuers and the next that publishes its terms in full: its personal credit card tariffs (in force from 1 May 2026), read in full: all its personal cards (American Express, Visa and Mastercard, local and international, Gold, Platinum, Infinite, AAdvantage and Bravo), each with its annualised interest rate (60%, 54% on the Visa Infinite, 48% on the Visa Infinite Banca Premium), written as a nominal yearly rate; the issue charge for the main card, set for the plastic's five years and charged as a yearly part, written as the yearly fee (the renewal at expiry costs the same and isn't written apart); the first year free on the American Express cards except the Suma CCN (whose 50% first-year discount isn't written); the cash advance commission (6.25%, 5.63% on the Infinite cards); the late fee in pesos and the overdraft fee in pesos, written as the late and over-limit fees (the Casa de Campo Platinum's overdraft fee reads RD$70, written as read; the dollar fees on dollar balances aren't written); the minimum payment, the interest, fees and charges plus a 36th of the capital, written as 2.78% of the balance plus the interest; and the 3% added to transactions in currencies other than the dollar, written as the foreign transaction fee. The optional insurance and the replacement charge aren't written. No grace period is stated. Tried and not used: Banco Caribe's and the Asociación Cibao's sites refused the request (403), Qik's home page answered but wasn't searched for a tariff in this pass, and Banco Lafise's didn't answer. Banco BDI was added too, a mid-sized bank whose tariff of products and services (modified 16 September 2026, in force from 15 October 2026) was read in full: its own-brand Visa Clásica, Gold, Platinum and Signature and its Anthony's co-branded Clásica, Gold and Platinum, each at 60% a year on peso balances; the issue charge for the main card, set for the plastic's five years and charged as a yearly part, written as the yearly fee (none on the own-brand Clásica, 'GRATIS'); the late (mora) and overdraft charges in pesos, written as the late and over-limit fees; a 6.00% cash advance commission; RD$1,500 for a returned cheque. The annual protection charge (a cover the tariff doesn't say is required) isn't written; the Crediplan, an instalment card at 30%, and the Santo Domingo Country Club cards, for the club's members, aren't written. No minimum payment, grace period or foreign transaction fee is stated.
